loudest.label: Service / version detection (banner grab)
signals: A connection that reads the service banner then disconnects
Occasionally a malformed/probe payload the service logs as a protocol error
loudest.quieter: Prefer the banner the service already volunteers; don’t send aggressive version-probe payloads unless the version genuinely matters.

loudest.label: HTTP method / CORS / header probe
signals: OPTIONS requests and cross-origin GETs — uncommon from real browsers, so they stand out under review
Requests carrying an unusual Origin header (CORS test)
loudest.quieter: A handful of targeted probes reveals the config; no need to sweep every method on every path.

loudest.label: Web crawl (following the site’s own links)
signals: Ordinary GETs for real, linked pages — no 404 flood (that’s the brute-force tell), but the volume and cadence from one source stand out under review
Full traversal of the navigable site in a short window, including deep paths real users rarely open
loudest.quieter: Cap pages and depth, pace requests with jitter, and let robots/sitemap seed the queue — a link-following crawl is already far quieter than path brute-force.

loudest.label: TLS configuration inspection
signals: One or a few TLS handshakes — ordinary unless you enumerate many cipher suites
loudest.quieter: A single handshake to read the negotiated config is plenty; skip exhaustive cipher enumeration unless required.

loudest.label: HTTP fingerprint (headers + favicon)
signals: A couple of ordinary GET requests (/, /favicon.ico) — indistinguishable from a normal visitor at low volume
loudest.quieter: Already low. A realistic User-Agent keeps it in the noise floor of ordinary traffic.

plan.issue: Malformed / injection payloads in requests (SQLi, traversal, deserialization) that WAFs and app logs capture verbatim
plan.quieter: Gate on a HIGH-confidence, confirmed finding; land the minimum proof rather than spraying payloads. This phase is HITL-gated for exactly this reason.

plan.issue: A burst of 404s (and the occasional 200/403) for paths a normal user never requests
plan.quieter: Use a focused wordlist seeded from robots.txt / sitemap / observed links, add jitter, and respect the app’s rate limits instead of hammering it.

plan.activity: Artifact written to a target host
plan.issue: A new file on disk (EDR file-create event)
plan.quieter: Drop the smallest possible proof, in an agreed location, and record it for cleanup immediately — VARVEL’s OPSEC ledger tracks it so it is removed on disengagement.

plan.issue: Requests for known-sensitive paths (/.git/HEAD, /.env, /actuator/env) — WAFs and SOC playbooks carry EXACT signatures for these, so each hit is conspicuous even at low volume
plan.quieter: Keep the probe list curated and high-signal (content-verified), pace requests, and let page audits ride on pages already fetched instead of adding volume.

plan.issue: One completed TCP handshake per open port (full connect, not a half-open SYN scan) — appears in firewall/flow logs and the service’s own connection log
plan.quieter: Scan only the ports the engagement needs, spread over time, from the authorized source; avoid full-range sweeps when a targeted set will do.
